result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.count_matches()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Count the matches of a Cypher MATCH pattern. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.count_matches()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Count the matches of a Cypher MATCH pattern. title: >- [Graph.count_matches()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Count the matches of a Cypher MATCH pattern. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Count the matches of a Cypher `MATCH` pattern. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L25478-L25580){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.count_matches( query, params=None, distinct_nodes=False, label_key="name", ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Count the matches of a pattern](/assets/graphs/count-matches.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A directed six-node grid A to F, where B and C point at each other and so do D and E; those four edges are in the accent color. The query MATCH (a)-->(b)-->(a) matches each 2-cycle once from each end, so the card lists B→C→B, C→B→C, D→E→D, and E→D→E, and the count is 4." width="100%"} This is the number of rows that `match()` would return for the same query, found without building the table. It's useful for motif counts, for checking that a pattern occurs at all, and in tests. See `match()` for the supported Cypher, how it reads the graph, and the matching rules. Counts follow Cypher, which matters for symmetric patterns: `(a)--(b)` matches each edge twice, once in each direction, and `(a)-->(b)<--(c)` counts each pair of edges into a node twice, as `a, c` and as `c, a`. A condition such as `WHERE id(a) < id(c)` counts each pair once. Each path of a variable-length relationship counts on its own, and a row that `OPTIONAL MATCH` filled with `null` counts as one match. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [query]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The Cypher text, such as `"MATCH (a)-->(b)-->(c)-->(a)"`. A `RETURN` clause is allowed; `RETURN DISTINCT`, aggregation (which gives one row per group), `SKIP` and `LIMIT` change the count, as they change the rows of `match()`, and so does `WITH`. Without `DISTINCT`, the columns of `RETURN` aren't computed, and with aggregation only the grouping keys are, so an expression that would raise an error in `match()` (such as `toLower()` of a number, or `sum()` of strings) doesn't raise one here. The columns of `WITH` are always computed. [params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[dict]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Values for the `$name` parameters in the query, as a dict such as `{"year": 1999}`. [distinct_nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, the nodes of a match must all be different, as in a subgraph isomorphism. The default follows Cypher, where only the edges must differ. [label_key]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["name"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The property that reads the node label when a node has no attribute of that name (`"name"` by default, matching `from_cypher()`), or `None` to read only attributes. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The number of matches. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the query is invalid, as for `match()`. [TypeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `query=` isn't a string, `params=` isn't a dict, or `label_key=` isn't a string or `None`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a directed graph, `(a)-->(b)-->(c)-->(a)` finds each directed triangle once per starting node, so three times: ::: {#063cff1f .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "C")]) ) graph.count_matches("MATCH (a)-->(b)-->(c)-->(a)") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: A pattern that returns to `a` still uses two different edges, so it finds the 2-cycle between C and D, once from each end: ::: {#baea860e .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.count_matches("MATCH (a)-->(b)-->(a)") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: Conditions in `WHERE` narrow the count. Here, the pairs of edges that leave the same node (only C has two): ::: {#6cecc542 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.count_matches("MATCH (a)-[r]->(), (a)-[s]->() WHERE id(r) < id(s)") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 1 ``` ::: :::
